chunks: Whoever desires that a pregnancy occur for him, let him pray two rak'ahs after the Friday prayer, prolonging the ruku' and sujud in both. Then he should say:

'O Allah, I ask You with what Zakariyya asked You: O Lord, do not leave me alone, and You are the Best of inheritors. O Allah, grant me from Your presence good offspring; indeed You are the Hearer of supplication.'

'O Allah, by Your Name I have made her permissible to me, and in Your trust I have taken her. So if You have decreed a child in her womb, make him a blessed, pure boy, and do not give Satan any share or portion in him.'

key_terms.أَمَانَتِكَ: Your trust/protection — refers to the sacred covenant of marriage undertaken in God's name
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً: Good/pure offspring — Quranic phrase from 3:38 in Zakariyya's prayer
key_terms.شِرْكاً وَلَا نَصِيباً: No share nor portion — prayer to completely exclude satanic influence from the child
key_terms.لَدُنْكَ: From Your own presence — Quranic phrase (3:38) indicating a direct gift from God
key_terms.يُحْبَلَ: Conception/pregnancy — specifically passive form meaning 'a pregnancy to occur for him'

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication in Islam for wanting to have a child?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches a specific ritual for those who wish to conceive children: two extra rak'ahs after Friday prayer with prolonged ruku' and sujud, followed by a supplication that incorporates the Quranic prayers of Prophet Zakariyya (21:89 and 3:38). The supplication then includes a declaration of the marital covenant made in God's name, a request for a blessed and pure son, and a prayer to protect the child from any satanic influence. This hadith belongs to the book on marriage in al-Kafi and reflects the Shia understanding that spiritual preparation accompanies physical intimacy.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from a man, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who intends that there be a pregnancy (of his wife) for him, so let him Pray two Cycles after the Friday (Prayers), with prolonged bowings and Prostrations in it. Then he should be saying,

‘O Allahazwj! I ask Youazwj with what Zakariyyaas had asked with. [21:89] Lord! Do not leave me alone; and You are the Best of inheritors. [3:38] Lord! Grant me from You good offspring; surely You are the Hearer of the supplication.

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! By Your<sup>azwj</sup> Name I have made her Permissible (unto me), and in Your<sup>azwj</sup>Entrustment that I take her. So if there is fulfilled for me a child in her womb, so Make it to be a boy, Blessed, Pure, and do not let Satan<sup>la</sup> neither have a participation in it, nor a share’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from a man from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘One who wishes for pregnancy should perform two Rak’at Salat (prayer) after Friday Salat (prayer) with long Ruku’ (bowing down on one’s knees) and Sajdah (prostration): then say, “O Lord, I ask and appeal before You as Zakariya had done. O Lord, do not leave me alone by myself -You are the best heir. O Lord, grant me from Your dominion fine offspring; You hear the prayer. O Lord, by Your name I have made her lawful and in Your trust I have taken her. If You have determined a child in her womb make it a son, a blessed one, [a clean one] and do not allow Satan to have a share or portion in him.’””
